potion_of_healing.name: potion of healing
potion_of_healing.lore: When Jeremiah asked whether there was no balm in Gilead, he spoke of the resin by which the traders of that hill country had long grown rich. The dungeon has a cheaper cousin to it, cave moss steeped in blessed spring water, which fizzes while it is fresh. One swallow will close cuts and take the ache out of bruises, and so the old delvers count their vials before ever they count their coins.

potion_of_extra_healing.name: potion of extra healing
potion_of_extra_healing.lore: The Samaritan who found a beaten stranger on the Jericho road poured oil and wine into his wounds, and this crimson syrup is brewed in the same spirit, though with a far bolder aim. It reaches beneath the skin to knit cracked ribs and settle bruised organs, and it tastes of iron and overripe cherries. The apothecaries who make it go red-fingered all their lives.

potion_of_full_healing.name: potion of full healing
potion_of_full_healing.lore: Athena gave Asclepius two vials of the Gorgon's blood. The blood from the left side killed, but with that from the right he raised the dead, and for so great a trespass Zeus answered him with a thunderbolt. What lies in this amber flask is very near to the blood of the right-hand vial. When it is drunk every wound closes at once, and for a breath the drinker remembers what it was to be whole.

potion_of_stamina.name: potion of stamina
potion_of_stamina.lore: Elijah lay down under a broom tree to die, but twice an angel woke him to eat a cake baked on coals, and in the strength of that food he walked forty days to Horeb. The poor man must make do with this green goo, rendered from beetle fat and ginger root. Its smell is appalling, but it will put the legs back under a starving delver.

potion_of_cure_poison.name: potion of cure poison
potion_of_cure_poison.lore: Mithridates of Pontus stood in such fear of poisoners that every day he swallowed a little of each venom he could find, until none could kill him. For nearly two thousand years physicians sold versions of his recipe under the name of theriac, and this pink fizz is an honest descendant of it, which hunts venom through the blood and leaves behind no more than an aftertaste of rose water.

potion_of_cure_disease.name: potion of cure disease
potion_of_cure_disease.lore: Naaman the Syrian came as a leper to Elisha, who bade him wash seven times in the Jordan. He grumbled that the rivers of Damascus were cleaner, yet at last he washed and came up with his skin like a child's. Less faith even than his is needed for this oily green draught, which burns out fever and the wasting sickness that eats away a delver's strength.

potion_of_cure_all.name: potion of cure all
potion_of_cure_all.lore: The Hippocratic Oath is sworn first by Apollo and Asclepius, by Hygieia and by Panacea, the daughter whose name means 'all-healing'. The alchemists pursued her through every furnace in Christendom, and none came nearer to her than the maker of this silver vial. It scours out poison, plague, blindness, dread and curse together, and leaves the drinker as clean as a rinsed cup.

potion_of_haste.name: potion of haste
potion_of_haste.lore: Hippomenes could not outrun Atalanta, so he rolled three golden apples across her path and won the race while she stooped to gather them. This frothing orange flask offers a fairer way to win, for whoever drinks of it moves swiftly while all the world behind wades as if through honey. Its froth will never settle, even in the stillest hand.

potion_of_invisibility.name: potion of invisibility
potion_of_invisibility.lore: A Lydian shepherd, as Plato tells, found a ring that hid him from sight and by its aid murdered his king and took the throne, and from that tale Plato asks who will stay honest when no one can see. This liquid is as clear as air and its flask seems empty. Whoever drains it will fade from view, and the blows that are aimed at the drinker will go wide.

potion_of_regeneration.name: potion of regeneration
potion_of_regeneration.lore: As often as Heracles struck a head from the Hydra two grew from the stump, until Iolaus seared the necks with a torch. This dark brew is distilled from creatures of that stubborn kind, from trolls and deep worms that grow again whatever they lose, and for as long as it lasts the drinker's wounds will close slowly and steadily, as water closes over with ice.

potion_of_heroism.name: potion of heroism
potion_of_heroism.lore: The heroes of Homer had their great hours, when a god breathed strength into one man and the line of battle bent around him, and in such an hour Diomedes wounded two of the gods. This golden draught, as thick as honey, will lend that hour to anyone, with arms that could bend iron and a heart to match them, though Homer makes it clear that every such hour must end.

potion_of_brilliance.name: potion of brilliance
potion_of_brilliance.lore: Odin desired a drink from Mimir's well, where wisdom lies, and gave an eye for it, since that was the price that Mimir set. This crystalline vial is a kinder bargain, for it costs nothing but itself and pours spent magic back into an emptied mind all at once, a far deeper draught than common mana.

potion_of_levitation.name: potion of levitation
potion_of_levitation.lore: The apocryphal Acts of Peter relate that Simon Magus rose into the air above Rome to prove his power, and that at Peter's prayer he came down far faster than he had gone up. The violet mist in this vial lifts its drinker but a hand's breadth off the floor, enough to pass clear of pits and snares, and when it fades it sets the drinker gently down.

potion_of_restore_strength.name: potion of restore strength
potion_of_restore_strength.lore: When the Philistines had shaved Samson and blinded him they set him to grind grain in Gaza, forgetting that his hair would grow again. As quietly does this bronze draught restore what was taken, for strength that sickness or sorcery drained away returns to the limbs in full. It does nothing for those who have lost nothing, and veterans count it a blessing when they have no need of it.

potion_of_gain_level.name: potion of gain level
potion_of_gain_level.lore: Jacob dreamed of a ladder set upon the earth with its top in heaven and angels going up and down upon it, and the stars that turn in this blue potion belong to that traffic. The drinker is lifted bodily to the floor above, nearer to daylight, though for one whose quest lies downward that may be no gain at all.

potion_of_fire_resistance.name: potion of fire resistance
potion_of_fire_resistance.lore: Nebuchadnezzar had his furnace heated seven times hotter and cast into it Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and they walked out without so much as the smell of smoke upon their clothes. No alchemist lays claim to such a miracle, yet this frost-white potion imitates it for a while, so that flame washes over the drinker and does only half its work, and dwarven smiths will sip of it before reaching into the forge.

potion_of_cold_resistance.name: potion of cold resistance
potion_of_cold_resistance.lore: At the southern edge of the first emptiness, as the Norse told, lay Muspelheim, the realm of fire, and from its sparks were made the sun and the stars. Something of that spark glows in this ember-orange vial. The drinker carries a hearth beneath the ribs, and frost that would blacken fingers settles on them as lightly as dew, which the frost giants hold to be a great insult.

potion_of_shock_resistance.name: potion of shock resistance
potion_of_shock_resistance.lore: Salmoneus of Elis dragged bronze kettles behind his chariot and flung torches into the air in mimicry of Zeus, until Zeus answered him with a true thunderbolt. This copper draught is for those who would sooner survive the lightning than imitate it. It is brewed with eel skin and lets a bolt pass through the body into the ground, leaving nothing but the taste of coins in the mouth.

potion_of_confusion.name: potion of confusion
potion_of_confusion.lore: The builders of Babel shared one language and one purpose, to raise a tower with its top in the heavens, until no man could understand his neighbor and the work was abandoned. This murky draught works the same confusion within a single skull, so that left and right change places, the feet go where they please and the plainest question arrives scrambled. Dishonest peddlers have been known to label it as a tonic.

potion_of_blindness.name: potion of blindness
potion_of_blindness.lore: Saul rode toward Damascus breathing threats until a light from heaven struck him blind, and for three days he was led by the hand like a child. The smoke that coils in this black vial has less to teach and does a smaller harm, for it shrinks the drinker's sight to arm's length until it clears. Yet in a dungeon already dark it is the last thing that anyone should wish to swallow.

potion_of_poison.name: potion of poison
potion_of_poison.lore: Locusta of Gaul was so skilled a poisoner that Nero kept her in his service and, as the historians relate, sent pupils to learn from her. Whoever bottled this purple ooze was schooled in that tradition, for it is spider venom thickened to cling on the way down and to burn a long while in the blood, and it gives no warning but its sliminess.

potion_of_paralysis.name: potion of paralysis
potion_of_paralysis.lore: Plato records how the hemlock took Socrates, and how he felt nothing when the jailer pinched his feet and then his shins, while the cold climbed on toward his heart. This ashen draught is ground from the cave mushroom called the Stillness Cap, and it stops short of the heart, leaving the mind wide awake within a body that will not answer. It passes quickly, though to the one who lies so it seems very long indeed.

potion_of_hallucination.name: potion of hallucination
potion_of_hallucination.lore: In medieval times the villagers who ate bread of blighted rye would see visions and feel their limbs burn. They named this sickness Saint Anthony's Fire and walked to his monks to be cured. The rainbow flecks in this flask work in the same fashion without any need of bread, so that walls breathe, shadows grow teeth, and no creature looks like itself until the colors drain away.

potion_of_sleep.name: potion of sleep
potion_of_sleep.lore: Ovid set the cave of Sleep where no rooster crows, with poppies at its mouth and the river Lethe whispering over the pebbles, and Hypnos once laid Zeus himself asleep as a favor to Hera. This flask is as warm in the hand as a cup held at bedtime, and in that comfort lies the snare, for no monster will wait until the sleeper has finished dreaming.

potion_of_weakness.name: potion of weakness
potion_of_weakness.lore: Delilah lulled Samson to sleep upon her knees and called a man to shave the seven locks of his head, and when he woke he went out to fight as before, not knowing that his strength had left him. This grey ooze works more swiftly and smells far worse, and until it wears off the drinker's blows land softly and the sword arm hangs heavy.

potion_of_slow.name: potion of slow
potion_of_slow.lore: Zeno of Elea argued that swift Achilles could never overtake a tortoise that had the start of him, since he must always first reach the place where it had been. No one believed him, but this violet potion makes his argument most persuasive, for it pours like cold tar and whoever drinks it moves in like manner, half a step behind every enemy in the room.

potion_of_teleportation.name: potion of teleportation
potion_of_teleportation.lore: When Philip had baptized the Ethiopian on the road to Gaza, the Spirit of the Lord caught him away, and he found himself at Azotus. This magenta flask grants such a journey but none of the guidance, for the drinker vanishes and arrives at some other place on the same floor, wherever the dungeon may choose. It has delivered many who were cornered, and has stranded quite as many who were careless.

potion_of_drain_strength.name: potion of drain strength
potion_of_drain_strength.lore: The giant Antaeus drew his strength from the earth, his mother, and no wrestler could throw him until Heracles lifted him clear of the ground and held him there while all that strength ran out. In like manner this storm-grey draught holds a man off the ground from within, and what it takes from his arms will not return of itself.

potion_of_drain_constitution.name: potion of drain constitution
potion_of_drain_constitution.lore: Eos begged Zeus to make her beloved Tithonus immortal, but she forgot to ask that he stay young, and so he withered year by year until little was left of him but a thin voice, and some say that he became a cicada. This brackish olive draught gives a taste of that bargain, for the drinker lives on and is lastingly less hardy.

potion_of_drain_wisdom.name: potion of drain wisdom
potion_of_drain_wisdom.lore: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart and received wisdom beyond that of any king, yet in his old age he let it slip from him and built shrines to the idols of his foreign wives. This bottle, patched of stone and clay and something like cured hide, was plainly made by one whose judgment had already gone. What is in it takes the same toll from the drinker, and what it takes will not return of itself.

potion_of_drain_intelligence.name: potion of drain intelligence
potion_of_drain_intelligence.lore: Odysseus sent three men to search out the land of the Lotus-Eaters, and when these had tasted the fruit all memory of home went out of them, so that he dragged them weeping back to the ships and tied them under the benches. A harsher vintage fills this mottled bottle, for it dulls the reasoning mind for good, and the drinker is rarely sharp enough afterward to count the loss.

potion_of_sickness.name: potion of sickness
potion_of_sickness.lore: The Iliad begins with a plague, when Apollo came down from Olympus like nightfall and for nine days shot his arrows into the camp of the Greeks, at the mules and dogs first and afterward at the men. One sulfur-yellow vial does the work of one such arrow, for its fever saps strength and hardiness by the hour, and it bears no honest label but the stench that comes through the stopper.

potion_of_fumbling.name: potion of fumbling
potion_of_fumbling.lore: The hagfish, when a shark has seized it, pours out slime enough in a heartbeat to choke the gills of its enemy, and then ties itself in a knot to wipe itself clean. This turquoise liquid has learned the first trick and not the second, so that hilts, straps and latches slip from the drinker's fingers at the worst moments, and all dignity along with them.

potion_of_fear.name: potion of fear
potion_of_fear.lore: The Greeks said that the god Pan could raise a shout to send whole armies running, and from him they named that feeling panic. The Athenians built him a shrine for the help he gave against the Persians at Marathon, and his shout is bottled in this wine-dark phial. The feet of anyone who drinks it will not go toward an enemy until the terror has run out.

potion_of_mana.name: potion of mana
potion_of_mana.lore: Fjalar and Galar the dwarves brewed the mead of poetry from honey and the blood of wise Kvasir, that whoever tasted it might make verses, and Odin stole it all away in three swallows. This azure brew of glowing cave fungus is humbler, yet its kinship to the mead is plain, for it refills the spent reserves of a mage and puts the spells back upon the tongue.

soma.name: Soma
soma.lore: The Rigveda gives an entire book, one hundred fourteen hymns, to Soma, which was pressed between stones and strained through wool, mixed with milk and offered to Indra before he fought the dragon Vritra. What plant it was the scholars still dispute, since the hymns tell only what it did. One draught of this honeyed gold will restore a broken body completely.

water_of_lethe.name: Water of Lethe
water_of_lethe.lore: On the banks of Lethe, as Virgil tells, Aeneas saw a multitude of souls drinking forgetfulness before their return to the world above, and Plato's Er, who watched the dead do likewise, noted that the unwise drank too deeply. A mouthful of this still water washes every affliction from body and mind, be it poison, fever, terror or curse, for what has been forgotten can linger no more.

elixir_of_gilgamesh.name: Elixir of Gilgamesh
elixir_of_gilgamesh.lore: Gilgamesh dove to the floor of the sea with stones tied to his feet and brought up a thorny plant that he named The Old Man Becomes Young, but as he bathed on the homeward road a serpent ate it and shed its skin. A sprig of it is steeping in this green bottle, and though it cannot give back lost years it will carry the drinker back one floor toward the daylight.

fafnirs_blood.name: Fafnir's Blood
fafnirs_blood.lore: When Sigurd roasted the heart of the dragon Fafnir for Regin, he burned his thumb upon it and put the thumb in his mouth. With that taste of the blood he understood the birds in the branches above him, who were talking of Regin's plan to murder him. The blood is scalding still, and what it gives depends upon the drinker, for the birds will tell a great deal to anyone who can follow their speech, and nothing at all to anyone who cannot.

draught_of_mimir.name: Draught of Mimir's Well
draught_of_mimir.lore: Beneath a root of the world-tree lies the well of Mimir, whose water is wisdom, and for a single drink of it Odin gave one of his eyes. This flask holds a mouthful, brought up by a trader who will not say what it cost him. The water will not stay in a fool, so that if you drink it you must think, there and then, or it will run straight through you and be gone.

potion_of_see_invisible.name: potion of see invisible
potion_of_see_invisible.lore: The king of Aram sent an army by night to seize the prophet Elisha at Dothan, and when morning came the prophet's servant saw the city ringed with horses and chariots and cried out. Then Elisha prayed that the young man's eyes be opened, and he looked again and beheld the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. This potion opens the eyes a little way toward such sight, so that for a while the drinker sees what walks unseen.

goatherds_coffee.name: Goatherd's Coffee
goatherds_coffee.lore: A goatherd, as the story goes, saw his goats dancing after they had eaten the red berries of a certain bush, and he carried some to the monks, who cast them into the fire in disgust. But at the smell of the roasting the brothers thought better of it and brewed a drink that held them wakeful through the night. A flask of it will keep any sleep off you, however it may come.
goatherds_coffee.drink_line: nothing can put you to sleep for 60 turns

nepenthe.name: Nepenthe
nepenthe.lore: At the table of Menelaus the talk of lost Odysseus made every man weep, until Helen slipped into the wine a drug given her in Egypt by Polydamna, the wife of Thon. Whoever drank of it, says Homer, shed no tear that day, though he saw his own brother cut down before him, and what it did then for grief it does in the dungeon for fear.
nepenthe.drink_line: fear leaves you, and nothing can frighten you for 50 turns

oil_of_rue.name: oil of rue
oil_of_rue.lore: Aristotle observed that a weasel eats wild rue when it goes to fight a snake, and the bestiaries said that by such means the little beast kills the basilisk, whose look is death to men. So herbalists press the bitter grey leaves into oil for all who must go where gorgons live, and when it has been rubbed upon the eyelids and the skin, nothing can turn the wearer to stone for a while.
oil_of_rue.drink_line: stone creeping in stops, and nothing can turn you to stone for 40 turns

fern_flower_tincture.name: Fern-Flower Tincture
fern_flower_tincture.unidentified_name: tall green vial with a red spark
fern_flower_tincture.lore: The Slavs told that on Midsummer night the fern blooms once for a single hour, with spirits guarding it from the unworthy, and that whoever plucks the flower can see where treasure lies hidden in the earth. Steeped in a drop of spirit, its petals keep a little of that sight.
fern_flower_tincture.drink_line: every treasure, chest and coin on the floor is marked on your map

moly.name: Moly
moly.lore: As Odysseus went alone to Circe's hall to save his crew, Hermes met him on the path and drew from the ground an herb that is hard for mortals to dig, black at the root and with a flower as white as milk, and by its virtue Odysseus drank her cup and remained a man. Steeped and bottled, moly keeps a mind its own, so that no glamour, muddle or false sight can take hold of it.
moly.drink_line: confusion, charm and false sight leave you and cannot take hold for 60 turns

theriac.name: Theriac of Andromachus
theriac.lore: Andromachus, who was physician to Nero, took the antidote of Mithridates and added to it the flesh of vipers, until his paste held some sixty-four things bound in honey. For seventeen centuries it was the great cure for poison, and in Venice it was compounded openly over forty days while officials kept watch on every jar. A dose of it will drive venom out of the body and keep it out.
theriac.drink_line: poison and disease are cured, and no poison can take you for 80 turns

water_of_epidaurus.name: Water of Epidaurus
water_of_epidaurus.lore: The sick who came to Epidaurus bathed in the sacred spring and lay down in the long hall of Asclepius to sleep and wait for the god to visit them in a dream, and the priests carved the cures in stone, telling of the blind who saw and the lame who walked out. Water drawn from that spring gives back whatever the dead and the diseased have taken from a body.
water_of_epidaurus.drink_line: every stat point a drain, a poison or a disease took from you comes back

charm_of_prometheus.name: Charm of Prometheus
charm_of_prometheus.lore: When King Aeetes set Jason to yoke two bronze bulls that breathed fire, Medea gave him the charm of Prometheus, an ointment from a flower that grew where blood fell from the Titan's side as the eagle tore it. Jason was anointed with it and walked into the fire unburnt, and the horns of the bulls bent against him like reeds.
charm_of_prometheus.drink_line: fire cannot hurt you for 30 turns, and blows land half as hard

water_of_the_styx.name: Water of the Styx
water_of_the_styx.lore: Thetis, as Statius tells, carried her baby son down to the river Styx and dipped him in it, so that no weapon could pierce him anywhere but in the heel by which she held him. For ten years Achilles fought at Troy without a wound, until an arrow found that heel. A few drops of the river will make a body like iron for a little while, but never in every part, for some heel is always left bare.
water_of_the_styx.drink_line: for 6 turns no blow, bite or claw can wound you, but an unseen blow finds the heel
